episode.title: Continue credential resolution after a higher-priority cached credential fails verification
episode.before: At parent c776c665b00a39d55c470beb788a2b9a77a2feb7, credential loading returned the first parseable object from the default cache path or GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS. Authentication then verified only that single object. Consequently, an expired or revoked default cached credential prevented a valid environment-specified credential from being considered. Encrypted storage also returned directly, bypassing any file-based fallback candidate.
episode.after: At f743ab579098f982d87ea3f2472c2405f6999297, credential sources are collected into an ordered list. The explicit cloud access-token override remains first; otherwise each cached candidate is verified sequentially using a credential-type-appropriate client. Verification failures are logged and resolution continues to the next candidate, allowing GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS to authenticate when a higher-priority cache entry is invalid. Successful default credentials still retain priority.
episode.diff: The change replaces a first-parseable-credential loader with an ordered candidate collector, adds tolerant encrypted-storage loading, generalizes non-authorized-user credential classification, factors consistent OAuth client construction and token-event handling, and changes initialization to verify candidates one at a time until one succeeds. It adds a regression test where an expired default refresh token is rejected and a valid GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS refresh token is subsequently selected. The commit modifies packages/core/src/code_assist/oauth2.ts and oauth2.test.ts with 167 insertions and 70 deletions.

evidence_units.claim: Pinned commit f743ab579098f982d87ea3f2472c2405f6999297 has parent c776c665b00a39d55c470beb788a2b9a77a2feb7, is titled "fix(core): sequentially verify cached credentials and restore GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS fallback (#28472)", and modifies the OAuth implementation and its tests.

Before the change, fetchCachedCredentials returned immediately on the first parseable credential object; the ordered paths placed the default cache before GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS, and encrypted storage was returned directly.

Before the change, initOauthClient verified only the single credential returned by fetchCachedCredentials; a caught verification failure then proceeded to later interactive or compute authentication logic rather than another file credential.

The replacement fetchCachedCredentialsList accumulates credentials in priority order, isolates load and parse failures per source, includes GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS after the default file when unencrypted storage is used, and returns all successfully parsed candidates.

initOauthClient now iterates through the ordered candidate list. Non-authorized-user typed credentials are adapted through GoogleAuth, while OAuth credentials are assigned to a newly configured OAuth2 client and checked with getAccessToken plus getTokenInfo. Errors are caught per candidate so the loop can continue.

A shared OAuth2-client factory preserves proxy configuration, token persistence, and post-authentication callbacks for the access-token override, every OAuth credential candidate, and later authentication flows.

The public getOauthClient entry point memoizes and invokes initOauthClient, so callers of the existing authentication API receive the revised ordered resolution behavior without an API signature change.

Existing credential-order tests establish that a valid default cache remains preferred, GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS is used when the default is missing, and typed external credentials are adapted through GoogleAuth.

The added regression test creates an expired default refresh token and a valid environment-file refresh token, makes token verification reject the default, invokes getOauthClient, and asserts that the environment credential is eventually assigned.

The committed regression oracle verifies the repaired transition from invalid higher-priority credentials to valid lower-priority credentials while the neighboring tests guard the intended priority and credential-type behavior. No test execution result was available from the inspected evidence bundle.

candidate_atomics.name: collect-ordered-credential-candidates
candidate_atomics.description: Collect all readable credential candidates in configured priority order, isolating source-specific loading failures so a later source remains available.

semantic_action.intent: Preserve credential-source priority without letting the first parseable or unreadable source erase later fallback options.
semantic_action.pre_state: Credential sources are configured, but resolution returns at most one parseable object and may bypass later sources.
semantic_action.post_state: Every successfully loaded credential is represented in an ordered candidate sequence, while a source-specific load or format failure does not stop collection.
semantic_action.validation: Priority tests show the default candidate precedes the environment candidate, while missing-default and invalid-default scenarios demonstrate that the environment candidate remains available.

candidate_atomics.name: verify-credential-candidates-until-success
candidate_atomics.description: Verify candidates sequentially with the appropriate authentication adapter, returning the first valid client and continuing after candidate-specific failure.

semantic_action.intent: Authenticate with a valid lower-priority credential when a higher-priority cached credential is expired, revoked, or otherwise unusable.
semantic_action.pre_state: An ordered sequence may contain an invalid higher-priority credential followed by a valid fallback credential.
semantic_action.post_state: The first candidate that successfully produces and validates an access token supplies the returned authentication client; a failed candidate does not terminate credential resolution.
semantic_action.validation: The regression test forces verification of the default refresh token to throw, then asserts that the valid environment-file credential is assigned; adjacent tests verify that a valid default still wins and typed external credentials use their dedicated adapter.

candidate_atomics.name: validate-invalid-primary-to-valid-fallback-transition
candidate_atomics.description: Exercise the resolution boundary with an expired primary credential and a valid secondary credential to prevent regression to first-candidate-only behavior.

semantic_action.intent: Establish an executable oracle for fallback after authentication failure rather than only fallback after absence or parse failure.
semantic_action.pre_state: Tests cover source priority, a missing primary source, and external credential adaptation, but not a present primary credential that fails token verification.
semantic_action.post_state: A test fails unless the resolver attempts the valid secondary credential after rejecting the expired primary credential.
semantic_action.validation: The mock authentication client throws for the expired refresh token, succeeds for the environment refresh token, and the assertion requires setCredentials to receive the fallback credential.

candidate_workflows.name: recover-authentication-through-ordered-credential-fallback
candidate_workflows.description: Resolve multiple credential sources without weakening source priority: collect all viable candidates, authenticate them sequentially using the correct adapter, and verify the invalid-primary/valid-secondary transition.

workflow_graph.goal: Return the highest-priority credential that actually authenticates, while retaining a valid lower-priority fallback when an earlier cached credential is unusable.
workflow_graph.entry_state: At least two credential sources may be configured, and a higher-priority source can contain a parseable but expired or revoked credential that previously blocked the lower-priority source.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Credential candidates retain their declared priority, each candidate failure is isolated, the first verified candidate supplies the client, and regression coverage distinguishes an invalid primary from a missing primary.
unresolved_or_deferred: The inspected regression test covers OAuth refresh-token candidates; fallback after a typed external-account candidate fails verification is implemented but not directly tested by the added case.
Encrypted-storage load failure is caught and the environment file remains collectable, but that specific branch is not directly exercised by the shown regression test.
Interactive-login and compute-metadata behavior after exhausting all candidates was not changed by the focal repair and is outside this workflow.
No cross-repository pattern is induced from this single ChangeEpisode.

unresolved_questions: The GitHub bundle contains no issue body, PR body, review discussion, comments, timeline, or status-check results, so implementation intent beyond the commit, diff, and tests cannot be independently attributed to discussion evidence.

No executed test result is present in the bundle, and the checkout had extensive pre-existing working-tree deletions; validation is therefore grounded in the committed test oracle rather than a fresh local test run.

The generalized rule treating every typed credential other than authorized_user as an ADC-style credential is visible in implementation, but the available tests directly demonstrate only the external_account_authorized_user case.
